questions.skill: Precise definition of an angle
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Write a precise definition of an angle. Name its vertex and its sides in your definition.
questions.prompt_markup: Write a precise definition of an angle. Name its vertex and its sides in your definition.
questions.correct_answer: An angle is the figure formed by two rays that have the same endpoint. The common endpoint is the vertex, and the two rays are the sides.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent wording. Essential: two rays (not lines or segments), one common endpoint, that endpoint named as the vertex. Not accepted: "the space between two lines", "a turn", or "two lines that cross" (two crossing lines form four angles).

questions.prompt: Sam writes: "An angle is the space between two lines." Explain two things that are wrong, and rewrite it as a precise definition.
questions.prompt_markup:
Sam writes: "An angle is the space between two lines."
Explain two things that are wrong, and rewrite it as a precise definition.
questions.correct_answer: Two crossing lines make four angles, so "two lines" does not name one angle; "space between" is not defined (an angle is the rays, not a region). Precise: an angle is the union of two rays with a common endpoint (the vertex).
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent answer. Essential: two errors (lines instead of rays or no common endpoint; a region instead of the figure) and a correct definition.

questions.prompt: A 1° angle is defined using distance around a circular arc. Complete the definition, and explain why the measure of an angle does not depend on the radius of the circle used.
questions.prompt_markup: A 1° angle is defined using distance around a circular arc. Complete the definition, and explain why the measure of an angle does not depend on the radius of the circle used.
questions.correct_answer: A 1° angle, with its vertex at the center of a circle, cuts off an arc that is 1/360 of the circle. Every circle centered at the vertex is cut in the same fraction, so the measure is the same for every radius.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent answer. Essential: vertex at the center, 1/360 of the circle, and the fraction (not the length) sets the measure.
